clue.text: Specific embargo relating to old capital

parts.note: the definite article marks out one particular thing, so specific gives the word 'the'
an embargo is a ban on trade

explanation.surface: A particular trade embargo that once applied to an ancient capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Specific' looks like an adjective on 'embargo', but it gives the definite article. Thebes was the ancient capital of Boeotia (and of Egypt), and its adjective is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was an ancient capital city, and the adjective formed from its name describes anything belonging to it.

clue.text: She sounds tight, the laughing creature

indicators.note: sounds says the word for drunk is heard, not spelt

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk, as is high
Ena stands for a woman, a 'she', as in the TV character Ena Sharples

explanation.surface: A woman giggling drunkenly like a cackling animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena Sharples was a formidable character in the long-running British TV soap Coronation Street.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted scavenger of Africa is known for a call that resembles human laughter.

clue.text: To do with the cleaning of the church?

definitions.text: To do with the cleaning of the church?

parts.words: To do with the cleaning of the church?
parts.note: suggests housework in a church building, but the washing meant is the sacramental one that cleanses a new member of the church

explanation.walkthrough: The 'cleaning' is the ritual washing with water that admits someone to the Christian church.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the rite of christening, a symbolic washing away of sin.

clue.text: Adjacent like the German in the Derby

parts.note: near means close or similar, as in a near likeness

indicators.note: what remains in the word Derby beside the German article, so that article is stripped away

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Something close by, compared with a German runner at the Epsom race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the' asks for what is left of Derby once DER, German for 'the', is taken off: BY. The Derby is a famous English horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means close at hand, next to something.

clue.text: Dog Latin as a mongrel form

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed into a new form

explanation.surface: Dog Latin is cobbled-together pseudo-Latin, described here as a mongrel version of the language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog Latin' reads as one phrase meaning bad Latin; in fact 'Dog' is the definition and 'Latin as a' is the fodder, shuffled to make the breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alsatian, or German shepherd, is a large breed of dog.

clue.text: Full of beans like an active footballer

definitions.meaning: a player who is living and booting the ball

explanation.surface: An energetic player compared to a lively person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means vigorous and lively, and literally describes a living player kicking a ball.

clue.text: Punishment that comes to a stop

definitions.meaning: a penalty passed by a judge
a grammatical unit that ends with a full stop

explanation.surface: A penalty that halts something.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's penalty and a grammatical unit ended by a full stop share the one word.

clue.text: Object of a night out

indicators.note: out signals the word night is put out of order

explanation.surface: The point of an evening on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a purpose; it is a noun for an item, and 'out' tells us to rearrange 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object or item.

clue.text: Command to turn dial through 180 degrees

definitions.text: Command to turn dial through 180 degrees

parts.words: Command to turn dial through 180 degrees
parts.note: a military order to face the opposite way, read playfully as rotating one's face, the 'dial', all the way round

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dial' is slang for a face, so turning the dial half a circle is reversing which way you face, the drill-square order.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the drill order to turn round and face the opposite way, also used of a complete reversal of policy.

clue.text: Attraction of West End panto time production

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter
a production is something made up or put together, so these letters are assembled afresh

explanation.surface: A London theatre's pantomime season is what draws the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but 'End' asks for the last letter of 'West', T, which joins PANTOTIME before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Temptation is the pull or allure of something desirable, an attraction.

clue.text: Pin-up in the lido, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word lido could be arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A glamour shot of someone at the open-air swimming pool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a British seaside fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an adored celebrity, the kind whose poster goes on a fan's wall.

clue.text: "Lest that thy love prove likewise —" (R and J)

definitions.text: Lest that thy love prove likewise

parts.note: the source is Romeo and Juliet, where Juliet begs Romeo not to swear by the inconstant moon, and the missing word completes her line

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with its last word left for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Juliet's balcony line ends 'Lest that thy love prove likewise variable', likening Romeo's love to the changing moon.
explanation.definitionFit: In the quotation the missing word describes something fickle and changeable, like the waxing and waning moon.

clue.text: Unlikely position of crew pressing hard

indicators.note: pressing means leaning up against, so the crew is placed right beside the letter for hard

parts.note: a rowing eight is the crew of an eight-oared boat
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A rowing crew pushing hard from an unpromising position in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a rowing crew; coming eighth is an unlikely place to finish if you hope to win.
explanation.definitionFit: Finishing in the place after seventh is a poor, unlikely spot for a contender to end up.

clue.text: Support with a smile

definitions.meaning: a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure

explanation.walkthrough: The printed answer is a misread: the two definitions both lead to the word for a girder and a grin.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam is both a load-bearing girder and a wide happy grin, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Learning I introduce about vanished Order

indicators.note: order is used as a verb here, telling us to put the letters into a new order
vanished means the letter for about disappears from the word introduce

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A scholar introduces a knightly order that has disappeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a chivalric body, but it is the anagram signal; 'vanished' takes C (about) out of INTRODUCE, leaving INTRODUE, which with I is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Erudition is deep scholarly knowledge acquired by study.

clue.text: Nominate Nye as a Saint

definitions.meaning: give a first name to Nye, the donkey of Walter de la Mare's poem whose full name is the answer
the bishop of Myra, patron saint of children and the origin of Santa Claus

explanation.surface: Proposing a politician named Nye for canonisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nye' suggests Aneurin Bevan, the Welsh Labour politician; in fact it is the surname in Walter de la Mare's poem title, whose first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's donkey is called by this forename, which is also borne by the saint venerated each December.

clue.text: Supervision done with sense

parts.note: something done or finished is over
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Supervising carried out sensibly.
explanation.walkthrough: The word has two opposite meanings: watchful supervision, and a failure to notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversight is the job of watching over and managing others' work.

clue.text: Outlaws company — it's going up and down

parts.note: a band is a company or group
taken as the word it

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as the word it a second time

explanation.surface: A gang of bandits whose fortunes rise and fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's going up and down' puts IT once as written (down) and once turned (going up), giving ITTI after BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the old Italian-style plural for bandits, lawless robbers.

clue.text: Defender unable to take more goes to rear

parts.note: someone who cannot eat another bite is full
back means towards the rear

explanation.surface: A footballer, already stuffed, drops back into defence.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby the full back is the defender playing furthest back.
explanation.definitionFit: A full back is a defensive player positioned at the rear of a team.

clue.text: Uniform given by the first Lady Newton

parts.note: in Genesis Eve is the first woman
N is the symbol for the newton, the unit of force

explanation.surface: Something about a uniform supplied by a titled woman named Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady Newton' looks like a peeress's title, but 'the first Lady' is Eve and 'Newton' is the unit symbol N.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means level and consistent throughout, which is what uniform means as an adjective.

clue.text: Box heavyweight for prize in Belmont

definitions.meaning: in The Merchant of Venice, Portia's suitors at Belmont choose among gold, silver and lead containers, the heavy lead one holding the prize, her portrait

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer fights for a prize at a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Belmont is Portia's estate in Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice; Bassanio wins her by choosing the lead one of three.
explanation.definitionFit: A casket is a small ornamental chest, and in Shakespeare's play the lead one held the winning portrait.

clue.text: Present newspaper boss is talented

parts.note: a present is a gift
ED is the abbreviation for editor, who runs a newspaper

explanation.surface: The current editor of a paper is a person of talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' reads as an adjective meaning current, but it is the noun meaning a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gifted has natural ability, so the word means talented.

clue.text: Put on ice extract of quinine drink

indicators.note: extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Chilling a quinine-flavoured mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'puT ON ICe'. Tonic water is flavoured with quinine.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a fizzy mixer flavoured with quinine.

clue.text: Suitable reading for three-year-olds?

parts.note: seems to mean books for toddlers, but the three-year-olds are racehorses, whose great flat races carry this collective name

explanation.walkthrough: In British flat racing the five Classics (the Derby, the Oaks, the St Leger and the two Guineas) are restricted to three-year-old horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Great works of literature are standard reading, and the major races for three-year-old horses share the name.

clue.text: Striking sound of Concorde

definitions.meaning: the ringing of a clock or bell as it strikes
agreement or harmony, the French spelling of concord

explanation.surface: The noise of the supersonic airliner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concorde' suggests the supersonic jet, but it means concord: to be in harmony is to be in this with someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell's peal is one sense; harmony or accord, as in being in tune with others, is the other.

clue.text: Evidence right on line say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: the sine was originally a line in a right-angled triangle, the half-chord set at right angles on the radius

explanation.surface: Proof that something is correct, found on the dotted line.
explanation.walkthrough: The trigonometric sine began as a length of line set at a right angle; spoken, it is identical to the word wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is an indication or trace that something is so, the same as evidence.

clue.text: Change one's opinion — transparent ruler has an advantage

parts.note: thin material can be seen through
K is the abbreviation for king
a gain is a benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: A see-through ruler on the desk offers some benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' suggests a measuring stick, given 'transparent'; it is a king, abbreviated K.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to revise a view one previously held.

clue.text: Drawing attention to criticism

definitions.meaning: rapping on a door to get someone to notice

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the rap at a door; the other is the informal word for carping disparagement.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapping at a door summons notice, and to run something down is to disparage it, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Kidnapped daughter named

parts.note: Kidnapped is the title of Robert Louis Stevenson's novel

explanation.surface: A girl abducted and then identified by name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kidnapped' looks like a verb acting on the daughter; it is the name of Stevenson's 1886 adventure novel, so it stands for 'title'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be called or given a name is to be designated, which titled can mean.
